text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Farooq Legahri said only a clean government which can provide good governance coupled with political stability and economic continuity should expect to complete its term in future.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index soared 4.11 percent in the pre-election session on strong speculative buying spurred by predictions of an election victory for Nawaz Sharif.
- The Supreme Court took possession of hundreds of audio tapes, scripts and other material regarding telephone tapping by the Intelligence Bureau during Benazir Bhutto's government.

- On the eve of the elections, major contenders in Larkana -- the bastion of Bhutto family -- ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto and her estranged sister-in-law Ghinwa Bhutto have refused to accept elections results if they are rigged.

- The international media is by and large predicting a hands-down Nawaz Sharif victory in the Monday's polls, but some sections are still doubtful whether the caretaker government will easily transfer power to the newly elected representatives.
- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association said the European Community's decision to impose anti-dumping duties on Pakistani textile exports is unjustifed and unfair.

- The Trading Corporation of Pakistan has cancelled the tender for the purchase of 25,000 tonnes sugar with India as its State Sugar Corporation failed to deliver the first consignment on time due to problem in railway system between the Indian city of Haryana and Wahga on Pakistani border.
- An overall improvement in tax administration and broadening of the General Sales tax will fetch an additional revenue of 66.25 billion rupees, sources said.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said his government has no favourites and will ensure fair and transparent polls.
